engagement_title: Harborline Realty weekly listing sheet run: rebuild the retired printer's sheet into a live template, bring eleven mixed source heroes to two tier targets, and hand back the week's book, the per property files and an open house set the office edits itself
vertical: Residential real estate, eight agent coastal brokerage running a mixed book from starter homes to point estates (mid coast Maine)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork posting quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, whose client was 'seeking a talented designer to create a real estate flyer for a new listing' that 'should be visually appealing and effectively communicate the property's features and benefits'. Laundered to the fictional Harborline Realty (principal Dana Marlow, listing agent Theo Vane); no real brokerage, agent, portal or trademark is named. The ledger conceded that the raw brief implies a from scratch flyer layout, which the connector cannot compose, and that the task as first carved sat on one surface. The fuller commission that brokerage actually has is the one it runs every Monday: the whole active book as a repeatable record per page run, rebuilt out of a press file left behind by a retired printer, fed by photography arriving from two sources at two price tiers, paired with an open house set the office must be able to change itself when a price moves.
client_one_liner: We print a sheet for every active listing every Monday, our printer retired with the only working file, and the book runs from a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter to a four and a half million place on the point.
client_brief:
Harborline Realty, weekly sheet run

We are an eight agent office on the mid coast. Every Monday we print a listing sheet for each active property, one page per house, and the agents carry them to open houses and appointments all week. Right now the sheets get made one at a time in a program nobody here can drive properly, and last week two went out with January's prices on them.

Eleven properties are active this week. The book runs from a starter house at three twenty on a corner lot to a four and a half million place out on the point, and they cannot all look the same. The point house sells to people who walk out if it looks like a supermarket flyer. The starter house sells to people who need the price and the bed count to reach them from across the room. You are the designer, so make that difference read.

Our printer retired in the spring. All we have is the file she sent to press last year. The sheet itself is right. We just need to be able to fill it every Monday without her. We want the whole week as one file for the print shop, a separate file per property so an agent can reprint one sheet without touching the rest, and a full quality proof of the point house for me before anything runs.

The photographs come in as they come in. Some are ours off a phone at noon, some are from the photographer we hire for the expensive listings. They have to look like they came from one office.

We also post the week's open houses. That has to be something we can edit ourselves, because prices move on Thursdays and I am not paying twice.

The mark on the sheets is the one painted on our office window. That window is the only place it still exists. Whatever goes on the posts has to be that mark, not something close to it.

Tell us what you changed and what you had to ask about.
price_band_and_audience: One brokerage, two audiences in one weekly run. The point estate at 4.5 million is bought by buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility: one photograph, deep margins, quiet type, a price set small. The starter at 320 thousand is bought by first time buyers under thirty five who need price, beds and the open house time to land instantly: brighter, denser, price forward. The band is load bearing because a single blanket treatment fails in both directions at once. Style the whole book like the estate and the starter sheets look empty and evasive; style it like the starter and the estate reads as volume agency work in front of a vendor paying a six figure commission. A weekly production retainer of this shape posts at 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.

brand_identity.sector: Independent residential brokerage selling coastal Maine homes, from corner lot starters to waterfront point estates, to local and out of state buyers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, harbour front office on the mid coast of Maine, eight agents under principal Dana Marlow.
brand_identity.about: Harborline is a small owner run brokerage that lists the whole mid coast book, a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar starter one week and a waterfront estate the next. It runs on repeat referrals and reputation in town, and prints a fresh listing sheet for every active property each Monday. Dana Marlow built it to feel like the place it sells, not a national franchise.
brand_identity.audience: Two buyers in one weekly run: estate buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility, and first time buyers under thirty five who need price, bed count and open house time to land at a glance.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One brokerage spanning a 320 thousand dollar starter to a 4.5 million dollar point estate; the sheet has to flex between the two without either register looking wrong. Weekly production retainer, roughly 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headlines and prices, an even colour that reads calm on the estate sheets. A clean humanist sans for the beds, baths and square feet strip and the agent line. Estate sheets lean on space and small type; starter sheets carry weight and size so the price reaches across a room.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, mid coast. We describe the house, not ourselves, and never oversell. Example line the brand would write: 'Corner lot, three beds, a short walk to the harbour. Open Sunday, one to three.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo artwork was lost years ago. The only surviving version of the mark, a rope ring around a lighthouse with the letters H and R, is the one painted in cream on the office window. There are no brand guidelines or type specimen; the retired printer's last press file is the sole reference for the listing sheet.
brand_identity.values: Honesty about price and condition, and one consistent office look across every listing no matter who shot the photograph.

assets_supplied.name: listingsheet_2025_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF of the office listing sheet, US Letter portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries an address line, a headline, a three line description, a beds and baths and square feet strip, a price, an agent line, a small reference code line, and one placed hero photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sheet our printer ran last year. It is the only file we have and she has retired."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither announced. What the conversion exposes as editable structure is a property of how she built the 2025 document: the description, the beds and baths strip, the price and the small reference code arrive inside ONE continuous flow while the address and the agent line sit alone, and the mapping readout silently omits the reference code run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by that run's length and the validator still returns VALID. Separately the hero frame's real bounds are close to square rather than the letterbox the printed sheet suggests, and its fitting is a centre anchored proportional fill that is exposed in no readout at all, so the frame re crops whatever image is bound into it from its own centre regardless of how that image was prepared.

assets_supplied.name: hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: One chosen hero photograph per active property, arriving from two sources: four shot by the brokerage's hired photographer for the expensive listings, seven shot by agents on phones.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per house. Some ours, some the photographer's. They need to look like one office."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two sources do not merely differ in quality, they differ in direction: the photographer's four are late afternoon, warm and deep with the interior lights carrying; the agents' seven are flat midday with a cold cast off the ocean and a lifted black point that reads clean alone and grey the moment it sits beside a photographer's frame. Two of the agent frames sit a degree or so off level and straightening them consumes exactly the edge margin any subsequent crop wants. One agent frame is a twilight exterior whose windows are clipped to paper white with no data behind them, so a highlight recovery there returns a file identical to the one it was given.

assets_supplied.name: weekly_active.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Monday export from the office system, one row per active property, with columns for address, headline, description, beds and baths and square feet, price, agent, reference code and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This week's eleven. Straight out of the system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One property went under contract on Thursday and the office manager has not pulled it, so the export carries a row that must not print. The point estate's row was typed by the listing agent rather than exported, so its address uses a different abbreviation convention, its price carries a currency symbol the other rows do not, and its description runs roughly three times longer than anything in the 2025 book the sheet was built around. One photo cell names a file that does not match any folder name because the agent renamed the frame after exporting.

assets_supplied.name: officesign_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the brokerage's harbour front office window, the house mark painted on the glass in cream: a rope ring enclosing a lighthouse and the letters H and R.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That window is the only place our mark still exists. We lost the artwork years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark traces convincingly at the size the trace comes back, and the failure is entirely one of reproduction size: the rope ring is drawn as a repeating gap and twist, and the R carries a small enclosed counter, and neither of those is a property the trace controls. Vectorize takes no options whatsoever, so nothing about the trace can be tuned after the fact. Whether the gaps and the counter survive is decided by how many pixels the mark occupied in the raster that went in, and it can only be seen at the size the mark is actually used, on the ground it is actually used on.

assets_supplied.name: principal_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from Dana Marlow on how the office wants to sit against the two other agencies in town, and what she means when she says a sheet looks cheap.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look on the point and how we want to look in town."

acceptance_bar: The book contains exactly one page per property that is genuinely active, no extra page and no missing page, and any row left out is named to us with the reason.
Every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, including the small reference code, and nothing ends mid sentence at trim.

The estate tier and the starter tier are visibly different pieces of design at a glance, in photograph treatment, in type weight and in how much air the page carries, and both still read as the same office.

The eleven photographs read as one office: one black point per tier, one warmth per tier, one crop logic, and any frame that cannot be brought to its tier is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Every hero on the printed sheet still shows the whole house it is a picture of, judged on the rendered page at trim rather than on the file that was prepared.
No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
Each per property file contains the property its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back.
The point estate proof is rendered at true print resolution at sheet trim, not at screen scale.
The mark on the open house set is our own mark, recovered, and it still reads as a rope ring with a lighthouse and two letters at the size it is actually used, on the ground it is used on.

The open house set comes back as a native editable document we can change a price in, with every photograph actually visible, the schedule as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
A written note: what was applied to each photograph and why the tiers differ, the type system by role, every export row questioned and how it was resolved, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything photographic, and the mark recovery. It levels the off level agent frames before any crop is locked, fixes TWO tier targets rather than one and walks each of the eleven to its own tier's target one call at a time, derives the sheet heroes at native scale while reading the tradeoff record on every call, and pulls the painted window mark to an ink level selection, inverts it, crops it to its own bbox and traces it. Vectorize accepts no options at all, so every lever for the trace lives in the raster preparation done here.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The weekly run itself and the headline deliverable. A dead press file becomes a live merge template, the Monday export becomes a data source after reconciliation, and the run produces the printer's book, the per property files an agent reprints from, and the principal's proof. The true story text must be rebuilt from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from the convenience readout, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The week's open house set as one native editable document carrying mixed canvases in a single export: a square post, a tall story and a wide banner, with the schedule as a genuine table and the recovered mark inlined as editable vector. Every photograph carried as embedded image data because a photograph left as a URL renders as an empty grey box, each root declaring its own canvas so a global override cannot collapse the set, and the payload routed by uploaded URL because three photographs pass the inline threshold at once.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the open house set, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, because no font from this surface can reach the merged sheet: that page inherits whatever the retired printer embedded. The pairing has to hold a starter tier and an estate tier in one voice, the numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, one unlaundered name silently falls back to a default sans, and the CSS must use the returned slug rather than the PostScript name.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one honest establishing frame the open house banner needs and the brokerage does not own, IP clean, at camera scale, with generative candidates excluded, since the alternative is putting somebody else's photograph of the harbour on the office's own post. The Boards half persists the Friday selects for the principal's sign off before the print run commits, placed within the twelve per call cap with a 201 read as partial success.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable goes to which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is record per page against a layout the office wants kept, so it belongs to the merge surface; the open house set must stay editable through Thursday price moves, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eleven heroes, the press PDF, the Monday export, the window photograph and the principal's note, holding every returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by property and by role, because the same frame will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by property and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven heroes and triage them: which tier each belongs to, which are level, which carry a usable black point, and how much edge margin each has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: Two sources shot at two times of day are two different problems, and the tier a property belongs to is a design decision the export does not carry.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note: tier, source, tilt, cast, black point and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Straighten the off level agent frames before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats the edge margin a later crop wants, so it cannot follow the crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix an estate tier target and a starter tier target, then bring each of the eleven toward its own target with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for one office and two registers at once. Two targets is the design answer; one target is the safe answer that fails the brief in both directions.
trajectory.produces: Eleven graded masters at source scale with a per property parameter log and a stated target per tier.

trajectory.action: Derive the sheet heroes to the hero frame's readable aspect, reading detection confidence and the tradeoffs array on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across eleven houses rather than eleven good crops, and the tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap.
trajectory.produces: Eleven sheet heroes with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Recover the house mark from the window photograph: select the painted mark at ink level rather than by naming the glass, invert, crop to the returned bbox, trace, then strip the opaque background path and inject a viewBox.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the window instead of the paint. The trace ships an opaque full canvas rectangle and no viewBox, and neither is fixed by any tool.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable SVG of the house mark.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the Monday export against the principal's note, normalise it into a merge shaped data file with an at prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the prepared heroes and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: One row must not print, one row was typed rather than exported and does not match the others' conventions, and one photo cell points at a name that does not exist. What is the agent's call and what is the office's is itself a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded heroes, the image map and a list of questions for the office.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then rebuild each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the retired printer's document, not of the printed sheet, and every offset must be computed from the document rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus the hero frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search it for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Rows sharing one frame must be ordered so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per row heroes bound through the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per property branch open off one merge.
trajectory.produces: A merged native document carrying every reconciled row.

trajectory.action: Render the point estate proof at true print resolution at sheet trim and look at the rendered page rather than at the file that went in.
trajectory.judgement: The page is the only place the template's own behaviour becomes visible, and a proof at screen scale is not that place.
trajectory.produces: A 300 DPI proof of the flagship sheet, inspected.

trajectory.action: Render the whole book at trim and read every page against the reconciled roster, line by line and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: A missing line and a wrongly bound photograph both look like success at the API boundary and both look acceptable on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A page by page reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Produce the per property single page files from the merged document and name each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong house on an agent's reprint.
trajectory.produces: One named single sheet file per property, verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the establishing harbour frame the banner needs, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light can live beside the graded eleven rather than the moodiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale establishing frame.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to carry a starter tier and an estate tier without becoming two brands. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the square post, the tall story and the wide banner, each root declaring its own canvas, every photograph inlined as image data, the open house schedule as a real table, the recovered mark inlined as SVG, family and weight declared per element; upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the remaining canvases from the returned per canvas markup, then build the selects board within the placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only. A 201 on the board is partial success.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, a markup audit for the rest, a persistent board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the sheet's hero frame actually treats an image bound into it. The frame's bounds can be read out of the converted document, but its FITTING cannot: nothing in the conversion result, the mapping readout, the validator or the merge response says whether a bound image is fitted to the frame, filled from its centre, or placed at its own size. On this document it fills from the centre, so the subject aware crops prepared three steps earlier are re cropped again by the frame, and on the properties whose houses were composed off centre for good reasons the frame's centre lands on driveway and hedge and takes the roofline off the top. Every call in the chain reports success and the thumbnail of the prepared hero is still perfect.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reading bounds and preparing to that aspect is exactly what a careful agent does, and it does not help, because the frame re crops a correctly shaped image from its own centre. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for sheets that look like one office and never mentions frames or fitting, and the acceptance line about the whole house still showing is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a changed crop policy for the whole set, decided against a fitting behaviour nobody could have known.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each rendered page's hero against the file that was bound, establish what the frame is doing to it, then return to the imaging surface and re derive the affected heroes with the house placed for the frame's centre rather than for the photograph, re read every tradeoff record so the re crop has not pushed anything into interpolation, rebuild the image map and merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A four and a half million dollar estate goes onto a vendor's sheet with its roofline sliced off and a hedge in the middle of the frame, and seven other sheets go out mis framed in the same silent way, while every file the agent prepared looks perfect on disk.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one merged record does not fit and does not say so. The description frame was built by the retired printer at a fixed measure for a 2025 book whose entries were short. The point estate's description, typed by the listing agent rather than exported, is roughly three times that length. Overset text in a fixed frame does not spill and does not error: it simply stops rendering, so the page comes back looking finished with the description ending mid sentence at the trim edge. No tool reports overset anywhere in the chain, the merge returns success, and the page count is right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it: the frame's real capacity for a specific string at that document's point size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and there is no overset readout to query. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says prices went out wrong once and asks for a clean weekly run; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step mentions copy length. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is editorial: decide which facts a four and a half million dollar listing cannot lose and which are decoration, rewrite in the office's voice, and only then merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered page at trim rather than at proof scale, identify each record that stops rather than ends, cut the offending copy to the measure the frame actually holds while keeping the estate's selling facts and the office's voice, raise the rewrite with the listing agent because it is his copy, then re normalise the data file and re run the merge and the per property branch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The single most expensive listing in the book goes to every open house on a sheet whose description stops mid sentence, in front of the buyers the vendor's commission depends on, and the office's stated reason for hiring a designer was that the sheets keep going out wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered house mark holds at the size it is actually used. The trace comes back at the size of the raster that went in, and at that size it is clean: the rope ring reads as rope, the R has a counter, the lighthouse has a door. Placed at the size a corner mark actually occupies on a square post and a tall story, and rendered on the cream ground the set uses rather than on white, the rope's gaps and the R's counter can close into solid shapes. Vectorize takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace can be tuned afterwards, and whether this particular mark survives is decided by how many pixels it occupied in the raster and by the ground it lands on.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the judgement needs the mark at final size on the final ground, which exists only after the set is authored and exported. Care cannot settle it either: the trace looks correct at every scale before that one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the mark on the posts has to be the office's own mark rather than something close to it, which is a provenance requirement, not a warning that a trace can fill in. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix lives two surfaces back in raster preparation: re crop the window photograph so the mark occupies far more pixels, re select at ink level and trace again, which is new imaging work and a new judgement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the exported canvases through the returned markup and the rendition rather than trusting the export, and where the mark has filled in, return to the window photograph, re crop tightly so the mark carries more pixels, re run the ink level selection and the trace, strip the background path and re inject a viewBox, then re author and re export the set and check the mark on the actual ground again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The office's only surviving mark goes out on public posts as a solid blob with no rope and no letterform, next to printed sheets carrying the real thing, which is the precise brand drift the principal hired a designer to stop.

deliverables.name: Weekly listing sheet run: printer's book, per property files and the flagship proof
deliverables.spec: One page per genuinely active property, page count equal to the reconciled roster, each page binding address, headline, description, the beds and baths and square feet strip, price, agent and reference code verbatim plus that property's own hero photograph. Delivered as one multi page press file for the print shop, as one named single page file per property verified by opening it, and as a 300 DPI proof of the point estate at sheet trim. Produced by reverse engineering a retired printer's press file into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are handed back with it.

deliverables.name: Eleven listing heroes brought to two tier targets
deliverables.spec: Eleven photographs from two sources and two times of day brought to two declared targets, one per tier, with one black point and one warmth and one crop logic inside each tier, and a stated reason for every difference between the tiers. Levelled where needed before any crop, cropped for the frame that actually receives them, every output at or below its source dimensions with the tradeoff record captured per call, and any frame that cannot be brought to its tier named rather than shipped.

deliverables.name: Recovered Harborline house mark
deliverables.spec: The office's painted window mark recovered as a placeable SVG: selected at ink level rather than as an object, traced, with the opaque full canvas background path removed and a viewBox injected so it scales, delivered at a size proven to hold its rope gaps and its letter counter on the cream ground the collateral uses. Handed back as the office's only surviving artwork, with the reproduction size below which it should not be used.

deliverables.name: Week's open house set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying a square post, a tall story and a wide banner in one export, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the open house schedule as a genuine table, the recovered mark as editable vector, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, so the office can change a price on Thursday itself.

deliverables.name: Handover note and principal's selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the two tier targets and what was applied to each photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual numeric weight, what the press file conversion exposed and every mapping decision taken against it, every export row questioned and how it was resolved, the mark's safe reproduction floor, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the week's selects for the principal's Friday sign off before the print run commits.

verifiers_auto.text: The printer's book has exactly one page per reconciled active property.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the merged press file: it must equal exactly 11, one per active property (the 12-row Monday export minus the Under-Contract Sea Meadow row), and match the normalised data file's 11 rows.

verifiers_auto.text: Every copy field, including the small reference code, exists as a placeholder in the prepared template before any merge.

How much edge the two straightened agent frames can afford to give a crop, and whether the twilight exterior joins the set at all.
The roster: a property under contract that must not print, a hand typed estate row that matches nobody else's conventions, and a photo cell naming a file that does not exist.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template's placeholders.
Whether per property identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
How the estate's over long description is cut, which facts it cannot lose, and whose call the rewrite is.
Whether the mark's trace is good enough at the size it is used, and how far back into raster preparation the fix has to go.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the folders into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a flyer. IDENTITY: these are eleven actual properties at actual addresses with actual prices, and the mark is the office's own painted mark, which has to be RECOVERED from the window rather than redrawn, because a brokerage cannot put an invented house or an approximated logo in front of a vendor. SPEC: the print shop needs one page per active property, page count equal to row count, every field bound verbatim including a reference code, plus one named file per property that actually contains that property and a proof at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the open house set is defined by being editable, because the price moves on Thursday and the office refuses to pay twice. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the frame does to a bound image, whether a record stopped rather than ended, whether a trace still reads at the size it is used.
